TAXONOMY: Node.js, Deno and Bun are application runtimes; V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore are language engines; JVM and CLR are managed virtual-machine/runtime specifications and implementations; Wasmtime/Wasmer/WasmEdge run WebAssembly; Cloudflare Workers/AWS Lambda/Vercel Functions are managed execution platforms. CODARIS should not flatten these into one type.

POPULARITY: State of JS runtime percentages are survey selections among JavaScript developers and can exceed 100% in total because respondents can use multiple runtimes. Stack Overflow's Node.js/Deno figures come from a different mixed web-technologies question. Keep the metrics separate.

Key_Relationships: JavaScript -> Node.js -> V8 -> native machine code
Node.js is not the JavaScript engine; V8 is its primary execution engine.
Deno adds runtime APIs, tooling and permissions around V8.
Browser runtime includes far more than the language engine.
Java/Kotlin/etc -> JVM bytecode -> JVM -> native execution
JVM is a specification with multiple implementations.
C#/F#/VB -> CIL -> runtime/JIT or AOT -> native
CLR/CoreCLR and .NET are related but not identical labels.
Elixir is a language; BEAM is the VM.
'Python' does not imply one runtime in every environment.
Wasmtime / Wasmer / WasmEdge / browser engine / others
Wasm is a binary instruction format, not itself a standalone runtime.
Wasm component -> WASI interfaces -> host capabilities
WASI defines interfaces/capabilities; the runtime enforces execution.

Methodology: Issue
CODARIS treatment
Why it matters
Runtime vs engine
Store separate Runtime Type and Engine/Host Relation fields.
Node.js is a runtime built on V8; Bun is a runtime built on JavaScriptCore; an engine is not the whole application runtime.
VM specification vs implementation
Treat JVM as a VM/specification family and HotSpot/OpenJ9/GraalVM as implementations/runtime distributions.
Prevents duplicate or misleading statements such as 'Java runs only on HotSpot'.
Managed vs native runtime
Include managed VMs and native language runtime systems, but label execution model and bytecode/IR.
Go, Haskell and Swift can have substantial runtimes even though application code is compiled to native code.
WebAssembly
Separate WebAssembly/WASI standards from concrete runtimes such as Wasmtime, Wasmer, WasmEdge and WAMR.
Wasm is an instruction format; WASI is a system-interface family; runtimes execute them.
Browser execution contexts
Keep Browser, Service Worker, Web Worker and Worklet entries as execution environments, not language engines.
State of JS explicitly measures some of these as JavaScript runtimes, but technically they sit above the JS engine.
Edge/serverless runtimes
Include major provider execution platforms but label them Managed execution platform.
They are relevant developer runtimes but also overlap the later CODARIS Cloud/Hosting category.
State of JS usage
Use the 2025 selections and calculated share of question respondents. Multi-select percentages can sum above 100%.
This is survey adoption among JavaScript-community respondents, not a global runtime market share.
Stack Overflow usage
Only include Node.js and Deno values where the Stack Overflow 2025 web-technologies question directly measured them.
Its denominator/question differs from State of JS, so values are not merged.
Country and gender
Do not infer runtime-by-country or runtime-by-gender shares from overall survey demographics.
Direct cross-tab data is required for defensible demographic claims.
Completeness
Describe this as an extensive curated catalogue of 581 entries, not every runtime ever built.
Runtime terminology overlaps engines, VMs, libraries, runtimes, historical implementations, research VMs, cloud execution contexts and hardware accelerators.
